labels.rationale: CLI is used as a defined contrast term with TUI, standard acronym pairing in this doc's domain.
Heading uses CLI consistently with the doc's established TUI/CLI terminology pair.
"Latest content" accurately names dynamic sync target, not a stale-prone product claim.
"Can see"/"hidden" are conventional, unambiguous technical idioms for filesystem visibility.
Same sentence mixes "you" and "the user" for the same referent, inconsistent reader address.
"This" summarizes the prior sentence's idea, a standard, recoverable usage, not ambiguous.
"Easy" is a flagged minimizing usability word per Google style word list; regex reliably catches it.
"This page covers" matches the canonical preannouncement pattern Google style bans.
"Detects"/"asks" plainly describe automated prompts, not misleading personification.
"It" in "compound it" has no explicit noun antecedent, only an implied complexity concept.
"Will degrade" predicts an outcome of a later translation step, a valid future-tense use.
Same pattern: predicts a translation-time consequence, not current tool behavior.
Consistently third-person description of general modal behavior, not mixed with "you."
"Just" accurately describes what a registry literally is, not a minimizing usability claim.
